newsitem.title: SPAIN: Swiss Novartis says merger smooth so far.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Novartis says merger smooth so far.

text.p: Swiss drugs giant Novartis AG has made a smooth transition after last year's merger, but the company must press ahead with rapid integration of its operations to keep productivity on course, the chairman said.
Ciba-Geigy and Sandoz merged last year to create pharmaceuticals and life sciences group Novartis, the world's second biggest drugs company behind Britain's Glaxo Wellcome Plc

Novartis chairman Alex Krauer told the daily Cinco Dias in an interview published on Thursday: "(The merger) has been much easier than I and other people thought it would be largely because during the negotiations prior to the announcement of the merger we had already reached a solid understanding of our objective".
However, he said the integration of the two companies must be concluded rapidly to keep the morale of the staff from waning.
"If it is prolonged this will be bad for results and the evolution of the company," he said.
Looking ahead to the 20th century, Krauer said the company wanted to be market leader in life sciences.
"We want to be the number one group in life sciences and be a high yield organisation."
